summary: The Petitioners, ACME Jodhpur Solar Power Private Limited and ACME Rewa Solar Energy Private Limited, have filed the present Petition seeking directions to the Respondents to reinstate the already reconciled amount pertaining to the Change in Law compensation towards GST Laws and Safeguard Duty Notification respectively payable to the Petitioners pursuant to the common order dated 5.2.2019 in Petition Nos. 178/MP/20218 and 189/MP2018 and the common order dated 2.5.2019 in Petition Nos. 342/MP/2019 and 343/MP/2018 of the Commission, respectively, and forthwith release the already deducted amount by the Respondents towards the same to the Petitioners. The Petitioners have made the following prayers: _(e) Pass any other order(s) or direction(s) as this Hon’ble Commission feels just and equitable in favour of the Petitioners.”_ _(b) Pass such other order(s) and further direction(s) as may be deemed fit and proper in the facts and circumstances of the present case.”_ 3. The Petition was admitted on 28.1.2025, and notice was issued to the Respondents permitting them to file their replies to the Petition as well as IA. Pursuant to this, Respondent No.2, Rajasthan Urja Vikas and IT Services Limited (RUVITL) and Respondents No.1, Solar Energy Corporation of India Limited (SECI) filed their replies on 22.5.2025 and 23.6.2025, respectively. The Petitioners have also filed their rejoinders thereon on 27.6.2025 and 1.7.2025, respectively. Thereafter, during the hearing on 8.7.2025, the learned counsels for the parties were heard at length, including on the issue of discrepancies/mismatches between the solar modules installed at the Project sites and the invoices submitted by the Petitioners. Considering their submissions, the Commission permitted the parties, i.e. the Petitioners, SECI and RUVITL, to resolve the issue amicably through a joint meeting within two weeks and submit the decision taken therein within two weeks thereafter. During the subsequent hearings on 26.8.2025 and 25.11.2025, it was informed that a joint meeting of stakeholders was convened on 4.8.2025 to explore an amicable solution to the issue(s) and that a joint committee was also constituted to undertake a fresh inspection of the Project sites. Accordingly, at the request of the Petitioners, as also supported by the Respondents, the hearing of the matter was deferred until the outcome of the above exercise. The parties were directed to file the outcome of the above exercise thereafter. 4. Accordingly, the Petitioners filed an additional affidavit dated 18.2.2026 apprising that the committee constituted by RUVITL conducted a joint site inspection and physical verification of modules installed at the respective Project site of the Petitioners on 14.10.2025, and during the course of the inspection, the Petitioners furnished all the requisite documents before the Committee in respect of their Projects. The Committee recommended that the duly signed brief and detailed reports of modules submitted by the Petitioners will be relied upon for ascertaining the total number of modules installed at the Projects. Subsequently, RUVITL and SECI reconciled the Change in Law claims of the Petitioners based on (a) brief and detailed reports of modules submitted by the Petitioner during the joint site inspection, and (b) invoices and supporting documents earlier submitted by the Petitioners in the year 2019-20. Pursuant to the above, the reconciliation process between the Petitioners, RUVITL and SECI has been concluded and payment of Rs. 9,93,16,692/- towards Change in Law on account of Safeguard Duty and Rs. 1,95,41,448/- towards Change in Law on account of GST, pertaining to the pre-Commercial Operation Date (COD) period, have been released in favour of the Petitioners. Thus, the Change in Law claims pertaining to the pre-COD period have been paid, and there is no dispute with respect to such pre-COD Change in Law claims. However, the Petitioners expressly reserve their right to claim compensation for Change in Law pertaining to the postCOD period in accordance with the outcome of the final order by the Hon’ble Supreme 5. Subsequently, during the hearing on 26.2.2026, the learned counsel for the Petitioners submitted that the issue(s) involved in the case have been resolved amicably and the Respondents have also made payment towards the Change in Law compensation for the pre-COD period of the Projects, and as such, there is no subsisting dispute with respect to the pre-COD Change in Law claims. Accordingly, the learned counsel submitted that the Petition may be disposed of while granting liberty to the Petitioners to claim the Change in Law compensation which has been deducted on account of invoices of the modules being after the COD of the Projects as per the outcome of Civil Appeal No. 8880 of 2022 and batch pending before the Hon`ble Supreme Court. The learned counsel for the Respondent, RUVITL, did not oppose the disposal of the Petition but objected to the grant of any such liberty to the Petitioners. 6. In view of the submissions of the Petitioners that their Change in Law claims for the pre-COD period have already been paid and that there is no subsisting dispute with respect to the pre-COD Change in Law claims, the grievance raised in the Petition no longer survives and accordingly, the Petition is disposed of as having rendered infructuous. It will be open to the Petitioners to raise any grievance with respect to the Change in Law compensation pertaining to the post-COD period after the outcome of Civil Appeal No. 8880 of 2022 & batch pending before the Hon`ble Supreme Court, which will be considered in accordance with the law.
